title: Microeconomics I
topics: Scarcity, choice and the economic problem

items.q: Price floor may be defined as
o: a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges
an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle
the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge
a resource whose amount can be changed at once as output rises or falls
items.s: Price floor: an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle. The other options describe Demand, Variable input, Cartel.

items.q: The statement “an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged” describes which of the following?
o: Variable cost
Implicit cost
Fixed cost
Average cost
items.s: Fixed cost is an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Production possibility frontier?
o: the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet
the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react
an item that many can enjoy at once and from which non payers cannot easily be kept out
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed
items.s: Production possibility frontier: a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed. The other options describe Determinants of elasticity, Choice, Public good.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rent?
o: a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision
the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work
the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
items.s: Rent: the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit. The other options describe Factor market, Collective bargaining, Free rider.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Determinants of elasticity?
o: the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react
the payment made for the use of human effort in the making of goods
a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute
the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power
items.s: Determinants of elasticity: the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react. The other options describe Monopoly, Wage, Income effect.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Opportunity cost?
o: an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available
a resource whose amount can be changed at once as output rises or falls
the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely
items.s: Opportunity cost: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken. The other options describe Oligopoly, Growth of capacity, Variable input.

items.q: The statement “the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal” describes which of the following?
o: Market equilibrium
Demand
Shortage
Price floor
items.s: Market equilibrium is the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal.

items.q: Rent may be defined as
o: the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want
a line joining the input combinations that can yield the same quantity of output
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed
the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
items.s: Rent: the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit. The other options describe Signalling role, Isoquant, Production possibility frontier.

items.q: Land may be defined as
o: a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor
the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods
the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods
the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
items.s: Land: the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods. The other options describe Market failure, Shortage, Factors of production.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Land?
o: the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item
the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods
the least return that keeps an owner in the business rather than moving elsewhere
items.s: Land: the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods. The other options describe Rent, Normal profit, Monopolistic competition.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Resource allocation?
o: the way a society settles how its limited means shall be divided among competing uses
the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires
the whole outlay spread over each unit of output
the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet
items.s: Resource allocation: the way a society settles how its limited means shall be divided among competing uses. The other options describe Average cost, Marginal analysis, Choice.
items.t: Scarcity, choice and the economic problem

items.q: Which term is described by “the way free bargaining between buyers and sellers settles what shall be made and for whom”?
o: Demand
Price ceiling
Price mechanism
Surplus
items.s: Price mechanism is the way free bargaining between buyers and sellers settles what shall be made and for whom.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Growth of capacity.
o: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
the payment made for the use of human effort in the making of goods
an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available
a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired
items.s: Growth of capacity: an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available. The other options describe Wage, Total utility, Explicit cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item”?
o: Total utility
Marginal utility
Indifference curve
Utility
items.s: Marginal utility is the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item.

items.q: Which term is described by “a grant from public funds that lowers what a buyer pays or raises what a seller keeps”?
o: Subsidy
Information asymmetry
Free rider
Government failure
items.s: Subsidy is a grant from public funds that lowers what a buyer pays or raises what a seller keeps.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Income elasticity of demand?
o: the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed
a combination of two goods that cannot be reached with the means and technique now available
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
items.s: Income elasticity of demand: how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households. The other options describe Production possibility frontier, Unattainable point, Price elasticity of demand.

items.q: Shortage may be defined as
o: the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it
the sacrifice of some of one objective in order to gain more of another
items.s: Shortage: the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling. The other options describe Tax incidence, Trade-off, Elastic.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Interest?
o: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
the extra output obtained by employing one more unit of an adjustable resource
the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
the return paid for the use of borrowed funds
items.s: Interest: the return paid for the use of borrowed funds. The other options describe Tax incidence, Total utility, Marginal product.

items.q: Utility may be defined as
o: the period in which at least one input cannot be varied
the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
the skill and health built into workers by education and training
items.s: Utility: the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service. The other options describe Income effect, Short run, Human capital.

items.q: Which term is described by “a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item”?
o: Product differentiation
Oligopoly
Monopolistic competition
Monopoly
items.s: Monopolistic competition is a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Price elasticity of demand?
o: the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed
the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands
the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes
items.s: Price elasticity of demand: the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes. The other options describe Long run, Implicit cost, Shortage.

items.q: Collective bargaining may be defined as
o: the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged
a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work
items.s: Collective bargaining: negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work. The other options describe Cartel, Ceteris paribus, Derived demand.

items.q: The statement “the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires” describes which of the following?
o: Marginal analysis
Unattainable point
Growth of capacity
Trade-off
items.s: Marginal analysis is the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Profit.
o: what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met
the addition to total outlay from making one more unit
the whole outlay spread over each unit of output
a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute
items.s: Profit: what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met. The other options describe Average cost, Marginal cost, Monopoly.

items.q: Surplus may be defined as
o: the period in which at least one input cannot be varied
the position in which sellers hold out more units than buyers are prepared to take at the charge now ruling
a claim about what is the case that can be checked against evidence
a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor
items.s: Surplus: the position in which sellers hold out more units than buyers are prepared to take at the charge now ruling. The other options describe Short run, Positive statement, Market failure.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Perfect competition?
o: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge
the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods
items.s: Perfect competition: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge. The other options describe Signalling role, Capital, Utility.

items.q: The statement “the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods” describes which of the following?
o: Choice
Microeconomics
Factors of production
Scarcity
items.s: Factors of production is the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods.
items.t: Scarcity, choice and the economic problem

items.q: Which term is described by “the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want”?
o: Market equilibrium
Price mechanism
Signalling role
Supply
items.s: Signalling role is the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Unattainable point?
o: the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
the principle that each further unit of an item taken in a given period adds less satisfaction than the one before
a combination of two goods that cannot be reached with the means and technique now available
describing a reaction in which buyers alter the units they take by a smaller proportion than the change in charge
items.s: Unattainable point: a combination of two goods that cannot be reached with the means and technique now available. The other options describe Inelastic, Marginal utility, Law of diminishing marginal utility.

items.q: Government failure may be defined as
o: a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction
describing a reaction in which buyers alter the units they take by a smaller proportion than the change in charge
the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better
a line joining the input combinations that can yield the same quantity of output
items.s: Government failure: the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better. The other options describe Inelastic, Indifference map, Isoquant.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Indifference curve?
o: a cost or benefit falling on people who were not party to a transaction
the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods
an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged
a line joining all the bundles of two goods that give a buyer the same level of satisfaction
items.s: Indifference curve: a line joining all the bundles of two goods that give a buyer the same level of satisfaction. The other options describe Factors of production, Externality, Fixed cost.

items.q: The statement “the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output” describes which of the following?
o: Variable input
Marginal product
Law of diminishing returns
Long run
items.s: Law of diminishing returns is the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Production possibility frontier.
o: the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
items.s: Production possibility frontier: a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Price elasticity of demand, Total utility.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Substitution effect?
o: the shift towards a cheaper item and away from a dearer one when relative charges change
a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely
the person who organises the other resources, bears the risk and decides what shall be made
the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
items.s: Substitution effect: the shift towards a cheaper item and away from a dearer one when relative charges change. The other options describe Entrepreneur, Opportunity cost, Oligopoly.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Implicit cost.
o: the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands
the way free bargaining between buyers and sellers settles what shall be made and for whom
the extra output obtained by employing one more unit of an adjustable resource
the need to allocate limited means among competing ends so that the greatest benefit is obtained
items.s: Implicit cost: the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands. The other options describe Price mechanism, Economic problem, Marginal product.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Government failure.
o: the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better
the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged
the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power
items.s: Government failure: the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better. The other options describe Price discrimination, Derived demand, Income effect.

items.q: The statement “the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge” describes which of the following?
o: Demand
Surplus
Price ceiling
Supply
items.s: Demand is the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Capital?
o: the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods
a line joining all the bundles of two goods that give a buyer the same level of satisfaction
the way output changes when every input is increased in the same proportion
items.s: Capital: man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods. The other options describe Factor market, Returns to scale, Indifference curve.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Opportunity cost?
o: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
the return paid for the use of borrowed funds
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed
the position in which sellers hold out more units than buyers are prepared to take at the charge now ruling
items.s: Opportunity cost: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken. The other options describe Surplus, Interest, Production possibility frontier.

items.q: Which term is described by “the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has”?
o: Budget line
Indifference map
Law of diminishing marginal utility
Utility
items.s: Budget line is the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Returns to scale?
o: the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged
the way output changes when every input is increased in the same proportion
the skill and health built into workers by education and training
a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired
items.s: Returns to scale: the way output changes when every input is increased in the same proportion. The other options describe Human capital, Ceteris paribus, Explicit cost.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Merit good?
o: the branch of study that examines the decisions of single households, single firms and individual markets
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
an item that society thinks people should have even if they would not choose it unaided
items.s: Merit good: an item that society thinks people should have even if they would not choose it unaided. The other options describe Factor market, Income elasticity of demand, Microeconomics.

items.q: The statement “a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute” describes which of the following?
o: Oligopoly
Product differentiation
Market structure
Monopoly
items.s: Monopoly is a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Perfect competition.
o: the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed
a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal
items.s: Perfect competition: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge. The other options describe Long run, Total utility, Market equilibrium.

items.q: Which term is described by “a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired”?
o: Explicit cost
Supernormal profit
Implicit cost
Marginal cost
items.s: Explicit cost is a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired.

items.q: The statement “the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands” describes which of the following?
o: Supernormal profit
Implicit cost
Variable cost
Average cost
items.s: Implicit cost is the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Oligopoly.
o: a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely
the sacrifice of some of one objective in order to gain more of another
what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met
the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
items.s: Oligopoly: a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely. The other options describe Profit, Trade-off, Derived demand.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Production function.
o: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge
an official upper limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed below the level trade would otherwise reach
the relationship between the amounts of inputs used and the greatest output obtainable from them
man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods
items.s: Production function: the relationship between the amounts of inputs used and the greatest output obtainable from them. The other options describe Price ceiling, Perfect competition, Capital.

items.q: Which term is described by “the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output”?
o: Marginal product
Law of diminishing returns
Production function
Short run
items.s: Law of diminishing returns is the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Positive statement?

a claim about what is the case that can be checked against evidence
the whole outlay spread over each unit of output
the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output
items.s: Positive statement: a claim about what is the case that can be checked against evidence. The other options describe Average cost, Law of diminishing returns, Price elasticity of demand.

items.q: Signalling role may be defined as
o: the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want
the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
the features of a line of trade that shape how sellers behave towards one another
items.s: Signalling role: the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want. The other options describe Marginal utility, Shortage, Market structure.

o: the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods
a claim about what is the case that can be checked against evidence
the branch of study that examines the decisions of single households, single firms and individual markets
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
items.s: Income elasticity of demand: how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households. The other options describe Factors of production, Microeconomics, Positive statement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Marginal utility.
o: the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output
the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better
the way a society settles how its limited means shall be divided among competing uses
items.s: Marginal utility: the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item. The other options describe Law of diminishing returns, Government failure, Resource allocation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Utility?
o: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
the sacrifice of some of one objective in order to gain more of another
an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
items.s: Utility: the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service. The other options describe Opportunity cost, Fixed cost, Trade-off.

items.q: Which term is described by “the need to allocate limited means among competing ends so that the greatest benefit is obtained”?
o: Scarcity
Resource allocation
Economic problem
Microeconomics
items.s: Economic problem is the need to allocate limited means among competing ends so that the greatest benefit is obtained.

a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute
an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle
a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision
items.s: Free rider: a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision. The other options describe Price floor, Monopoly, Isoquant.

o: the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge
the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal
the addition to total outlay from making one more unit
the way a society settles how its limited means shall be divided among competing uses

items.q: Which term is described by “a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision”?
o: Information asymmetry
Market failure
Free rider
Government failure
items.s: Free rider is a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision.

o: a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place
a resource whose amount can be changed at once as output rises or falls
an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available
the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge

items.q: The statement “the amounts of a good that sellers are ready to put on the market at each possible charge” describes which of the following?
o: Price mechanism
Supply
Shortage
Surplus
items.s: Supply is the amounts of a good that sellers are ready to put on the market at each possible charge.

items.q: Which term is described by “the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged”?
o: Perfect competition
Price discrimination
Monopoly
Cartel

the shift towards a cheaper item and away from a dearer one when relative charges change
the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged
a return above the minimum needed to keep the owner in that line of business
items.s: Substitution effect: the shift towards a cheaper item and away from a dearer one when relative charges change. The other options describe Marginal product, Supernormal profit, Ceteris paribus.

o: the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal
a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely
the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
the position in which sellers hold out more units than buyers are prepared to take at the charge now ruling
items.s: Market equilibrium: the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal. The other options describe Oligopoly, Marginal utility, Surplus.

o: Law of diminishing marginal utility
Marginal utility
Total utility
Utility
items.s: Total utility is the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together.

Human capital
Collective bargaining
Rent
items.s: Rent is the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit.

describing a reaction in which buyers alter the units they take by a smaller proportion than the change in charge
the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the way free bargaining between buyers and sellers settles what shall be made and for whom
items.s: Derived demand: the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make. The other options describe Inelastic, Human capital, Price mechanism.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Normative statement?
o: the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
a state in which one side of a bargain knows much more than the other
the human effort, both physical and mental, that is applied in making goods and services
a judgement about what should be done, resting on values that evidence alone cannot settle
items.s: Normative statement: a judgement about what should be done, resting on values that evidence alone cannot settle. The other options describe Shortage, Information asymmetry, Labour.

o: a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges
the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes
describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it
the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has
items.s: Price elasticity of demand: the degree to which the number of units taken moves when the item's own selling charge changes. The other options describe Budget line, Cartel, Elastic.

a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor
a cost or benefit falling on people who were not party to a transaction
the principle that each further unit of an item taken in a given period adds less satisfaction than the one before
items.s: Law of diminishing marginal utility: the principle that each further unit of an item taken in a given period adds less satisfaction than the one before. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Externality, Market failure.

o: Profit
Interest
Human capital
Factor market
items.s: Factor market is the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them.

o: Income elasticity of demand
Inelastic
Tax incidence
Cross elasticity
items.s: Income elasticity of demand is how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households.

o: Microeconomics
Scarcity
Factors of production
Resource allocation
items.s: Scarcity is the condition in which the means available are not enough to satisfy every claim made on them.

a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
a line joining the input combinations that can yield the same quantity of output
items.s: Total utility: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together. The other options describe Fixed cost, Isoquant, Explicit cost.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Monopoly.
o: the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
the return paid for the use of borrowed funds
a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute
the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
items.s: Monopoly: a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute. The other options describe Interest, Tax incidence, Opportunity cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available”?
o: Opportunity cost
Growth of capacity
Trade-off
Production possibility frontier
items.s: Growth of capacity is an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available.

items.q: In this course, Monopoly refers to
o: the making of an item seem distinct by brand, design or service so that buyers stop treating rivals as identical
the features of a line of trade that shape how sellers behave towards one another
a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges
a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute
items.s: Monopoly: a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute. The other options describe Market structure, Product differentiation, Cartel.

items.q: The statement “the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better” describes which of the following?
o: Government failure
Subsidy
Externality
Market failure
items.s: Government failure is the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Isoquant means.
o: the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed
the principle that adding more of one adjustable resource to a fixed one eventually yields smaller and smaller extra output
a line joining the input combinations that can yield the same quantity of output
a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place
items.s: Isoquant: a line joining the input combinations that can yield the same quantity of output. The other options describe Fixed input, Law of diminishing returns, Long run.

items.q: Which term is described by “the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling”?
o: Shortage
Price floor
Signalling role
Surplus
items.s: Shortage is the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling.

items.q: In this course, Rent refers to
o: what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met
the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
the payment made for the use of human effort in the making of goods
the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
items.s: Rent: the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit. The other options describe Profit, Wage, Factor market.

items.q: In this course, Factors of production refers to
o: the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet
the condition in which the means available are not enough to satisfy every claim made on them
the way a society settles how its limited means shall be divided among competing uses
the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods
items.s: Factors of production: the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods. The other options describe Scarcity, Resource allocation, Choice.
items.t: Scarcity, choice and the economic problem

items.q: Which term is described by “describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it”?
o: Tax incidence
Determinants of elasticity
Elastic
Inelastic
items.s: Elastic is describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it.

items.q: In this course, Variable cost refers to
o: the whole outlay spread over each unit of output
the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands
a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired
an outlay that rises and falls with the quantity turned out
items.s: Variable cost: an outlay that rises and falls with the quantity turned out. The other options describe Average cost, Explicit cost, Implicit cost.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the extra output obtained by employing one more unit of an adjustable resource”
o: Marginal product
Short run
Law of diminishing returns
Returns to scale
items.s: Marginal product is the extra output obtained by employing one more unit of an adjustable resource.

items.q: The best definition of Utility among these is
o: the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction
items.s: Utility: the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service. The other options describe Budget line, Indifference map, Marginal utility.

items.q: All of the following belong to Costs, profit and the firm EXCEPT
o: Implicit cost
Explicit cost
Fixed cost
Externality
items.s: Every other option belongs to Costs, profit and the firm. “Externality” belongs to Market failure and government intervention, not Costs, profit and the firm.

items.q: In this course, Variable input refers to
o: a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place
a resource whose amount can be changed at once as output rises or falls
the period in which at least one input cannot be varied
the relationship between the amounts of inputs used and the greatest output obtainable from them
items.s: Variable input: a resource whose amount can be changed at once as output rises or falls. The other options describe Short run, Fixed input, Production function.

items.q: The statement “a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction” describes which of the following?
o: Utility
Marginal utility
Income effect
Indifference map
items.s: Indifference map is a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction.

items.q: Utility is best described as
o: the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has
the shift towards a cheaper item and away from a dearer one when relative charges change
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power
items.s: Utility: the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service. The other options describe Budget line, Income effect, Substitution effect.

items.q: Price discrimination is best described as
o: a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item
a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges
the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged
the features of a line of trade that shape how sellers behave towards one another

items.q: The statement “the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service” describes which of the following?
o: Indifference map
Income effect
Indifference curve
Utility
items.s: Utility is the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item”
o: Market structure
Oligopoly
Monopolistic competition
Perfect competition
items.s: Monopolistic competition is a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Market equilibrium means.
o: the function of changing rewards in passing information to producers about what buyers want
the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal
the position in which sellers hold out more units than buyers are prepared to take at the charge now ruling
an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle
items.s: Market equilibrium: the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal. The other options describe Signalling role, Price floor, Surplus.

items.q: The best definition of Shortage among these is
o: an official upper limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed below the level trade would otherwise reach
an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle
the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge
the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
items.s: Shortage: the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling. The other options describe Price ceiling, Price floor, Demand.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods”
o: Entrepreneur
Labour
Normative statement
Capital
items.s: Capital is man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods.

items.q: Which term is described by “man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods”?
o: Capital
Normative statement
Ceteris paribus
Labour
items.s: Capital is man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods.

items.q: Elastic is best described as
o: how far the amount taken of one item shifts when the selling charge of a different item moves
describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
items.s: Elastic: describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Cross elasticity, Tax incidence.

items.q: Which term is described by “what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met”?
o: Factor market
Derived demand
Wage
Profit
items.s: Profit is what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Price mechanism and market equilibrium?
o: Supply
Price mechanism
Monopolistic competition
Demand
items.s: Every other option belongs to Price mechanism and market equilibrium. “Monopolistic competition” belongs to Market structures, not Price mechanism and market equilibrium.

items.q: The best definition of Free rider among these is
o: a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision
a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor
the outcome in which official action leaves matters worse rather than better
an item that society thinks people should have even if they would not choose it unaided
items.s: Free rider: a person who benefits from something without contributing towards its provision. The other options describe Government failure, Market failure, Merit good.

items.q: Marginal analysis is best described as
o: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires
a combination of two goods that cannot be reached with the means and technique now available
the sacrifice of some of one objective in order to gain more of another
items.s: Marginal analysis: the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires. The other options describe Unattainable point, Trade-off, Opportunity cost.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Land means.
o: the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods
the human effort, both physical and mental, that is applied in making goods and services
man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods
the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged
items.s: Land: the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods. The other options describe Capital, Labour, Ceteris paribus.

items.q: The statement “how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households” describes which of the following?
o: Inelastic
Tax incidence
Elastic
Income elasticity of demand
items.s: Income elasticity of demand is how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute”
o: Monopoly
Oligopoly
Cartel
Market structure
items.s: Monopoly is a trade with a single seller of an item that has no close substitute.

items.q: Production possibility frontier is best described as
o: the value of the next best alternative given up when a decision is taken
an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available
the practice of comparing a small extra benefit with the small extra sacrifice it requires
a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Marginal utility means.

the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has
the satisfaction a person derives from consuming a good or a service
items.s: Marginal utility: the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item. The other options describe Utility, Budget line, Substitution effect.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place”

Marginal product
Short run
Fixed input
items.s: Fixed input is a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges”
o: Product differentiation
Price discrimination
Monopolistic competition
Cartel
items.s: Cartel is a group of firms that agree to act as one in settling amounts and charges.

items.q: Production function is best described as
o: a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place
the period in which at least one input cannot be varied
the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed
the relationship between the amounts of inputs used and the greatest output obtainable from them
items.s: Production function: the relationship between the amounts of inputs used and the greatest output obtainable from them. The other options describe Long run, Fixed input, Short run.

items.q: Which term is described by “a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction”?
o: Income effect
Law of diminishing marginal utility
Utility
Indifference map
items.s: Indifference map is a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction.

the branch of study that examines the decisions of single households, single firms and individual markets
the broad classes of resources, namely land, labour, capital and enterprise, that are combined to make goods
the condition in which the means available are not enough to satisfy every claim made on them
items.s: Economic problem: the need to allocate limited means among competing ends so that the greatest benefit is obtained. The other options describe Factors of production, Microeconomics, Scarcity.

items.q: Derived demand is best described as
o: the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
the skill and health built into workers by education and training
the payment made for the use of human effort in the making of goods

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met”
o: Derived demand
Interest
Human capital
Profit
items.s: Profit is what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met.

items.q: Which term is described by “an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged”?
o: Explicit cost
Fixed cost
Variable cost
Normal profit
items.s: Fixed cost is an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged.

items.q: In this course, Supernormal profit refers to

the addition to total outlay from making one more unit
an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged
a return above the minimum needed to keep the owner in that line of business

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the making of an item seem distinct by brand, design or service so that buyers stop treating rivals as identical”

Product differentiation
Monopolistic competition
Monopoly

a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item
the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged
the features of a line of trade that shape how sellers behave towards one another
items.s: Monopolistic competition: a trade with many sellers offering slightly different versions of an item. The other options describe Price discrimination, Product differentiation, Market structure.

items.q: The statement “the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power” describes which of the following?
o: Income effect
Utility
Substitution effect
Marginal utility
items.s: Income effect is the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power.

items.q: The best definition of Collective bargaining among these is
o: the skill and health built into workers by education and training
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work
the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
items.s: Collective bargaining: negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work. The other options describe Human capital, Factor market, Derived demand.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Factor market means.
o: the skill and health built into workers by education and training
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work
the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
the return paid for the use of borrowed funds
items.s: Factor market: the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them. The other options describe Human capital, Collective bargaining, Interest.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged”

Ceteris paribus
Labour
Entrepreneur
items.s: Ceteris paribus is the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged.

Price elasticity of demand
Cross elasticity
items.s: Determinants of elasticity is the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react.

a judgement about what should be done, resting on values that evidence alone cannot settle
the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods
the assumption that every influence other than the one under study is left unchanged

items.q: Tax incidence is best described as

the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
how strongly the number of units taken reacts to a shift in the spending power of households
the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react
items.s: Tax incidence: the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Determinants of elasticity, Cross elasticity.

the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged
the making of an item seem distinct by brand, design or service so that buyers stop treating rivals as identical

items.s: Price discrimination: the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged. The other options describe Oligopoly, Monopoly, Product differentiation.

items.q: In this course, Normative statement refers to

man made goods such as tools, machines and buildings that are used in making other goods
the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods
a claim about what is the case that can be checked against evidence
items.s: Normative statement: a judgement about what should be done, resting on values that evidence alone cannot settle. The other options describe Capital, Land, Positive statement.

items.q: Collective bargaining is best described as
o: the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the return for the use of a natural resource such as farmland or a mineral deposit
what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work

Information asymmetry
Free rider
Subsidy
items.s: Merit good is an item that society thinks people should have even if they would not choose it unaided.

Market failure
Public good
Free rider
items.s: Market failure is a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor.

o: Supernormal profit
Normal profit
Variable cost
Fixed cost
items.s: Normal profit is the least return that keeps an owner in the business rather than moving elsewhere.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available”
o: Marginal analysis
Unattainable point
Trade-off
Growth of capacity
items.s: Growth of capacity is an outward movement of the boundary caused by more or better means becoming available.

the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction
the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has
items.s: Income effect: the change in the amount taken that follows from a change in a person's real purchasing power. The other options describe Indifference map, Marginal utility, Budget line.

items.q: Market equilibrium is best described as
o: the amounts of a good that sellers are ready to put on the market at each possible charge
the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal
the position in which buyers seek to take more units than sellers are offering at the charge now ruling
the amounts of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible charge
items.s: Market equilibrium: the position at which the amounts buyers seek and the amounts sellers offer are equal. The other options describe Demand, Supply, Shortage.

items.q: All of the following belong to Market structures EXCEPT
o: Market structure
Normative statement
Monopoly
Perfect competition
items.s: Every other option belongs to Market structures. “Normative statement” belongs to Resources and economic method, not Market structures.

items.q: The statement “the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet” describes which of the following?
o: Economic problem
Choice
Resource allocation
Scarcity
items.s: Choice is the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet.

Indifference curve

items.q: Which term is described by “the whole outlay spread over each unit of output”?
o: Fixed cost
Marginal cost
Normal profit
Average cost
items.s: Average cost is the whole outlay spread over each unit of output.

items.q: Which term is described by “negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work”?
o: Collective bargaining
Factor market
Wage
Profit
items.s: Collective bargaining is negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work.

o: a case in which free trade produces an outcome that society judges to be poor
an item that many can enjoy at once and from which non payers cannot easily be kept out
a grant from public funds that lowers what a buyer pays or raises what a seller keeps
a state in which one side of a bargain knows much more than the other

items.q: Which term is described by “the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together”?

Income effect

Determinants of elasticity
Tax incidence

the branch of study that examines the decisions of single households, single firms and individual markets
the act of deciding which claim to meet with limited means, so that another is left unmet
the condition in which the means available are not enough to satisfy every claim made on them

Indifference curve
Income effect

items.q: Which term is described by “the amounts of a good that sellers are ready to put on the market at each possible charge”?
o: Signalling role
Price ceiling
Supply
Market equilibrium
items.s: Supply is the amounts of a good that sellers are ready to put on the market at each possible charge.

the trade in which households offer resources and firms hire them
the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
the payment made for the use of human effort in the making of goods

an outlay that does not vary with the level of output while the plant is unchanged
the least return that keeps an owner in the business rather than moving elsewhere
a payment actually made to outsiders for a resource that is hired

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the set of combinations of two goods that exactly exhaust the means a person has”

Budget line
Indifference map
Income effect

an outlay that rises and falls with the quantity turned out
the addition to total outlay from making one more unit
the least return that keeps an owner in the business rather than moving elsewhere
items.s: Implicit cost: the value of a resource owned by the firm and used in its own business without any payment changing hands. The other options describe Variable cost, Normal profit, Marginal cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “a boundary showing the greatest output combinations obtainable when all resources are fully and efficiently employed”?
o: Opportunity cost

Marginal analysis

the wish to hire a resource that arises only from the wish for what it helps to make
negotiation between an employer and a body representing its staff over the terms of work
items.s: Profit: what remains of takings once every other claim on them has been met. The other options describe Collective bargaining, Derived demand, Interest.

items.q: The correct meaning of Elastic is
o: how far the amount taken of one item shifts when the selling charge of a different item moves
the sharing of the burden of an official levy between buyers and sellers
the features of a good, such as the number of substitutes and its share of spending, that fix how buyers react
describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it
items.s: Elastic: describing a reaction in which the change in units taken is proportionately greater than the change in charge that caused it. The other options describe Tax incidence, Determinants of elasticity, Cross elasticity.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle”
o: Price ceiling
Signalling role
Market equilibrium
Price floor
items.s: Price floor is an official lower limit on what may lawfully be charged, fixed above the level free bargaining would settle.

items.q: “the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods” is the definition of
o: Positive statement
Capital
Land
Ceteris paribus
items.s: Land is the natural resources supplied by nature, including soil, water, minerals and climate, used in making goods.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Perfect competition.
o: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge
a trade dominated by a few large sellers who watch one another closely
the charging of different amounts to different buyers for the same item although the outlay is unchanged
the making of an item seem distinct by brand, design or service so that buyers stop treating rivals as identical
items.s: Perfect competition: a model of trade in which very many small sellers offer an identical item and none can affect the charge. The other options describe Product differentiation, Oligopoly, Price discrimination.

items.q: “the whole outlay spread over each unit of output” is the definition of
o: Implicit cost
Average cost
Explicit cost
Fixed cost
items.s: Average cost is the whole outlay spread over each unit of output.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Total utility?
o: a set of such lines drawn together, each standing for a higher or lower level of satisfaction
a line joining all the bundles of two goods that give a buyer the same level of satisfaction
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together
the addition to satisfaction gained from taking one more unit of an item
items.s: Total utility: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of an item consumed together. The other options describe Indifference map, Indifference curve, Marginal utility.

items.q: Long run may be defined as
o: a resource whose quantity is frozen while the present plant stays in place
the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed
the way output changes when every input is increased in the same proportion
the period in which at least one input cannot be varied
items.s: Long run: the span in which every resource can be adjusted and none is held fixed. The other options describe Fixed input, Short run, Returns to scale.
